title: SQL Upsert Patterns: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
realWorldScenario: A telemetry service aggregates daily page views per user. If the record for today does not exist, insert it with count = 1; if it already exists, increment the existing count by 1.
questionStatement: Write the PostgreSQL `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` statement to achieve this atomic upsert. Why is this superior to executing `SELECT` followed by `INSERT` or `UPDATE` in application code?
hints: Use the EXCLUDED keyword to access the values that were proposed for insertion.
